newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica's NBS Boland sees growth in its first year.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica's NBS Boland sees growth in its first year.

text.p: Newly created banking group NBS Boland said it was well placed to improve earnings in its first financial year despite difficult operating conditions expected at this stage of the financial year.
"The board is confident that the group is well placed to meet the challenges of a fast changing financial services market.

We remain above the regulatory capital requirments and have sufficient capital to allow solid growth over the next few years," NBS Holdings chief executive officer Tony Norton said in a statement accompanying NBS results.

NBS reported a 31 percent increase in headline earnings per share to 407.4 cents for the year ended March from 310.1 cents in the previous year. Dividends jumped 30 percent to 130 cents from 100 cents.
Board of Executors Ltd, NBS and Boland Bank Holdings Ltd have joined forces to create South Africa's fifth largest banking group.
BOE announced on March 13 that it had decided to buy 22.2 percent of NBS while NBS Boland would buy 24.3 percent of BOE and its shareholding of the new group would fall to 17.2 percent.
